title: Edge-Optimized YOLOv11n Architecture for Offline Recognition of Nigerian Sign Language Alphanumeric Gestures
abstract: arXiv:2611.00025v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Deaf inclusion across sub-Saharan society faces regional hurdles, with Nigeria as the core empirical focus. Existing recognition models demand heavy computational infrastructure. However, standard mobile phones used locally rarely exceed 1 GB to 4 GB of RAM. This study addresses constraints through a lightweight YOLO11n object-detection framework. The system provides real-time Nigerian Sign Language recognition for low-resource hardware. A benchmark dataset containing 11,208 raw gesture images was established. The data spans 33 static classes collected from five signers. Partitioning isolates signers S1 through S3 for training. Signer S4 provides validation data. Signer S5 is reserved for testing. Spatial augmentations are restricted strictly to the training set. This yields 23,509 training images. translated_title: 面向边缘优化的YOLOv11n架构：用于尼日利亚手语字母数字手势的离线识别
translated_abstract: 撒哈拉以南非洲社会中聋人群体的融入面临区域性障碍，其中尼日利亚是本研究的核心实证焦点。现有的识别模型需要繁重的计算基础设施，然而当地使用的标准手机内存很少超过1GB至4GB。本研究通过一个轻量级的YOLO11n目标检测框架来解决这些限制，该系统为低资源硬件提供实时的尼日利亚手语识别。研究建立了一个包含11,208张原始手势图像的基准数据集，数据涵盖从五名手语者收集的33个静态类别。数据划分方面，手语者S1至S3用于训练，手语者S4提供验证数据，手语者S5保留用于测试。空间数据增强严格限制在训练集内，最终产生23,509张训练图像。验证集和测试集在多种环境下各包含1,681张图像。该框架集成了量化感知压缩技术。
tldr: 本研究提出面向边缘设备优化的轻量级YOLOv11n架构，并建立了包含11,208张图像、33个静态手势类别的尼日利亚手语基准数据集（按手语者严格划分训练、验证与测试集），实现了在内存仅1至4GB的低资源移动硬件上对尼日利亚手语字母数字手势的实时离线识别。
en_tdlr: This study proposes an edge-optimized lightweight YOLOv11n architecture and establishes a benchmark dataset of 11,208 images spanning 33 static gesture classes (with signer-independent training, validation, and test splits), enabling real-time offline recognition of Nigerian Sign Language alphanumeric gestures on low-resource mobile hardware with only 1–4 GB of RAM.
